meta.scope: title through 'What round 5 should attack first' (Appendix A's normative scope); 'Verified in scratch' and 'Cost' excluded as measurement records
meta.extraction: one atom per sentence, list-item sentence, table row, or pseudocode function (the revision-8 algorithm, re-run on the revision-9 text)
meta.reconciliation: Appendix A, 'The classified lists are spec data' (GAP-27). Rule 1: an atom containing a sentence of rev9/appendix_a/wide_claims_classified.json takes that list's class and witness string (several sentences in one atom: the P/D/C ones win, else the longest). Rule 2: every other atom is classed by Appendix A's table: the section rules for N, G, S, H and D, the Preamble (a summary of the design) is S, and within the mechanism sections a heading, list introduction or statement about an earlier revision or a critic is H, a measured CPython fact citing a probe is C, and the rest is P. Its witness is the case, gate clause, invariant, model property or control it names; else, for a sentence citing a revision-9 gap, the witnesses of that gap's row in the Revision 9 table; else those its enclosing paragraph, list item or row names; for C a probe also counts. Rule 3: every P, D or C atom with no witness has needs_witness true and is a Revision 9 follow-up gap in SPEC_GAPS.md. The revision-7 list was not read (outside the exam author's allowed reading), so atoms whose wide-list row defers to it (class 'old') are classed by rule 2 and marked class_source 'rule2_table_rev7_list_unread'.

classes.C: a fact about CPython the design relies on
classes.G: rule a gate/harness/exam author must follow
classes.H: history, rationale, heading or quoted earlier claim

rules.section: Decisions where the judges disagree
rules.text: question: Keep 3.11 (setprofile adapter)? | judge 1: Refuse 3.11; one adapter | judge 2: "Put the panel question on the record": refuse 3.11 if L-SIGNAL-311 is py310-class | decision and reason: **Refused.** L-SIGNAL-311 is py310-class. A Python-level profile hook turns every C call on a sectioned thread into a point where CPython *skips the call* when an asynchronous exception lands there. That corrupts the traced program: the harness's own `with lock:` release is skipped and other threads hang. It was measured on D1's 3.11 adapter at 3606/50385 SIGALRM timeouts (D1), 2238/31329 (judge 2) and 1458 leaks in 4 s (judge 1), against 0 untraced. This is the mechanism of round-4 BLOCKER hook-exception-leaves-lock-held, whose fix sketch was "no profile hook when a C lock method is called", and no 3.11 hook can meet that. SIGNAL_TIMER covers only the detectable precondition: SIGINT, handlers installed mid-section and pthread_kill remain. The cost is real and disclosed as over-blocking #6: 3.11 is the lab's default interpreter, and the P1 retro and the exam move to 3.12/3.13.

rules.section: Decisions where the judges disagree
rules.text: question: 3.11 f_lasti pairing for every target (judge 2 graft 1) | judge 1: — | judge 2: Required if 3.11 is kept | decision and reason: Moot, because 3.11 is refused.

rules.section: Decisions where the judges disagree
rules.text: question: A test-only fault hook (judge 2 graft 2) | judge 1: Not asked | judge 2: "plus a test-only fault hook" | decision and reason: **No hook in production code.** A test branch in the hot path would itself be mutation surface. Instead a frozen, read-only `_v5_faultpoints()` returns `{qualname: code}` for every machinery function. The frozen injector (sys.monitoring INSTRUCTION/LINE events on tool id 5) and the exam's lower-id fault tool (id 3, PY_START) take their targets from it. This meets judge 2's aim: the exam and the SM instruments read no private name except `_v5_state()` and `_v5_faultpoints()`.

rules.section: Decisions where the judges disagree
rules.text: question: SM2 attainability | judge 1: UNDISTINGUISHED reported, not gated; D3's ≤3% not adopted | judge 2: EXAM_HOLE = 0 attainable only with a normalizer restricted to spec-fixed observables; mask N ≥ 5 | decision and reason: **Both are adopted** (revision 1: exactly N = 5, and UNDISTINGUISHED is never judged equivalent). The two positions do not conflict. An exam frozen before the implementation can only assert what the spec fixes, so SM2 compares only spec-fixed observables. Anything else a mutant changes is UNDISTINGUISHED, reported with its diff and handed to round 5.

rules.section: Decisions where the designs disagree and no judge ruled
rules.text: question: PEP 562 attribute whose product differs between two calls | decision: **UNRESOLVED** (D3). Not D1's NOT_A_FUNCTION, not D2's UNSTABLE_ATTRIBUTE | reason: The name does not resolve to one object. NOT_A_FUNCTION stays about the *kind* of object, and no new code is needed.

rules.section: Decisions where the designs disagree and no judge ruled
rules.text: question: Fork | decision: **Pass-through** (D1): in another pid, `run()` just calls fn | reason: Fork-pool jobs keep working. Child work was never credited.

rules.section: Decisions where the designs disagree and no judge ruled
rules.text: question: Cache wrappers | decision: **Accepted through the real callee** (D1/D3), not refused (D2) | reason: Sound once identity comes from `gc.get_referents`. D2's `.__wrapped__` remedy is kept for the refusals.

rules.section: Decisions where the designs disagree and no judge ruled
rules.text: question: Generator and coroutine targets | decision: **Supported with confirmed credit** (D1/D3), not refused (D2) | reason: Confirmation makes their counts sound on 3.12/3.13 (synth/p_confirm_frame.py; D3 p1/p4).

rules.section: Decisions where the designs disagree and no judge ruled
rules.text: question: `'<'` co_filename | decision: **Accepted, pinned residual R05b** (D1, judge 1), not refused (D2) | reason: Refusing would refuse every dataclass `__init__` (V05) for a deliberate-only residual.

rules.section: Decisions where the designs disagree and no judge ruled
rules.text: question: THREAD_HOP note | decision: **Retired** (D3) | reason: With no per-thread hook there is no post-hop blind spot to report.

rules.section: Decisions where the designs disagree and no judge ruled
rules.text: question: Tool id lifetime | decision: **Kept for the process** (D1), not released (D3) | reason: Monotone state has fewer crash prefixes. The cost to other tools is disclosed.

rules.section: Decisions where the designs disagree and no judge ruled
rules.text: question: Tool id preference | decision: **4, then 3** (D3) | reason: Callbacks for one event run in ascending tool-id order. Leaving 3 free lets a lower-id tool (the exam's fault tool, a debugger) act first; X135 depends on this.

rules.section: Decisions where the designs disagree and no judge ruled
rules.text: question: Tool name (revision 1) | decision: `_TOOL_NAME = "styxx.protocol/" + os.urandom(6).hex()`, drawn once per loaded copy of the module | reason: `_ensure_tool` adopts only an id that carries *this copy's* name. A second copy of `styxx.protocol` in one process, such as an exec'd copy as the lab's runners use, takes the other id or refuses MONITOR_BUSY. It never overwrites the first copy's callbacks (R1-B4). **Revision 2 (N8):** `importlib.reload(styxx.protocol)` is not a second copy. It re-runs the module in the same globals, and M1's state is bound with `globals().get(...)` semantics, so the reload keeps the registries, the tool id and this name. Revision 1's plain bindings lost held mints and used up a tool id per reload (`rev2/p10_reload.py`).

rules.section: Decisions where the designs disagree and no judge ruled
rules.text: question: Per-thread registry (`_TH`) | decision: **Deleted** | reason: With no hook to install, it served only the 3.11 adapter and diagnostic parity. Uncredited diagnostics are now counted on every thread.

rules.section: Decisions where the designs disagree and no judge ruled
rules.text: question: Pending-entry key | decision: `m.pend[id(frame)] = (frame, entry_offset, outcome)`, **holding the frame**, per mint (not D3's global bare-id map) | reason: While an entry is pending, its frame id cannot be reused. Retiring a mint drops its entries in one `clear()`.

rules.section: Decisions where the designs disagree and no judge ruled
rules.text: question: Where asyncio is imported | decision: In `coverage_trace()` (the constructor), never at `styxx.protocol` import and never inside `__enter__` or `__exit__` | reason: Scoring-only users do not pay for the import, and no *machinery* import runs inside enter or exit. The one import inside `__enter__` is the declared module's, at E3: resolution, outside the mutex, before anything global is touched, and a documented user-code site (L-ASYNC-EXC). D1 showed that an interrupted `import asyncio.events` inside `__enter__` leaves importlib's module lock held on 3.11.

rules.section: Delta from v5e, section by section
rules.text: v5e section: **Target identity: rule** | v5f change: Unchanged in meaning: `f_code is M_T` and `f_globals is F_T.__globals__`. A frame now *counts* only once confirmed (Attribution).

rules.section: Delta from v5e, section by section
rules.text: v5e section: **Resolution** | v5f change: Branches on the real type (`issubclass(type(obj), ModuleType / type)`, `type(obj) is staticmethod or type(obj) is classmethod`) and never reads `obj.__class__`. No type test is a tuple membership: `in` compares with `==`, which runs a metaclass `__eq__` (revision 1). Own dicts are read only through C descriptors; a Python-level `__dict__` descriptor stops the step or walk and is never called. staticmethod and classmethod are unwrapped at every step. PEP 562 `__getattr__` is called twice and the two products must be identical (else UNRESOLVED). INHERITED searches the whole MRO. A `sys.modules` entry that is not a ModuleType refuses UNRESOLVED. Only the import and the PEP 562 calls have an `except Exception` (chained UNRESOLVED); nothing else has a handler.

rules.section: Delta from v5e, section by section
rules.text: v5e section: **F_T selection** | v5f change: For a C cache wrapper, F_T is its *real callee* (the unique FunctionType among `gc.get_referents(wrapper)`), which must be the own-dict `__wrapped__`. Also refused: a callee bound by name in the module or the holder, and a sibling cache wrapper of the same callee there. New: RESERVED_TARGET for `Handle._run`, `BaseEventLoop._run_once`, or any function whose code is a cut code (revision 2 adds `_run_once`).

rules.section: Delta from v5e, section by section
rules.text: v5e section: **Provenance** | v5f change: The declared module must have an exact-str, non-`.pyc`/`.pyo` `__file__`. Every FunctionType link the walk visits, F_T included, must be *coherent*: its `co_filename` starts with `'<'`, or its realpath/normcase equals that of its own globals' `__file__`. The walk steps through the own-dict `__wrapped__` of *any* object, and from a cache wrapper to its real callee. It stays bounded at the object plus 16 hops and cycle-detected. The FOREIGN_DEFINITION message names the innermost `module:qualname`.

rules.section: Delta from v5e, section by section
rules.text: v5e section: **Aliases** | v5f change: Accepted only when the declared *objects* are identical. Different declared objects that reach one F_T refuse NOT_A_FUNCTION.

Each mint records `gc.get_freeze_count()`. Entry CODE_SWAPPED fires only against a mint that still has a live holder (reconciliation runs first).

rules.section: Delta from v5e, section by section
rules.text: v5e section: **Tripwires** | v5f change: CLONE_CALLED and CODE_SWAPPED are checked for *every* holder. CLONE_ALIVE adds the freeze clause: the gc freeze count *rose* since the mint was made. rules.section: Delta from v5e, section by section

rules.section: Delta from v5e, section by section

A str-subclass section is normalized with `str.__str__`; any other non-str section refuses UNDECLARED_SECTION without being compared. The NESTED_SECTION text now distinguishes a same-section opening from a different-section one. rules.section: Delta from v5e, section by section
rules.text: v5e section: **Close and exit** | v5f change: THREAD_HOP and PROFILER_LOST are retired. Closing is one claim (`o.fin.setdefault`) plus idempotent cleanups. Exit is a claim, then a credit stop, detach, a transaction under the mutex, the tripwires, and a final commit.

rules.section: Delta from v5e, section by section
rules.text: v5e section: **Mechanism** | v5f change: Revision 8: the registration reads its exchanges through `itertools.tee`, so a replaced callback is released only after its count. Revision 7: an exit whose registration repairs a callback that a party replaced counts it in `_LOST`, E4 counts a re-take of its own id like a rebinding, and the binding check runs at every `coverage_trace()`. `_LOCK`, `_ACTIVE`, `_STOP`, `_THREADS`, `_EPOCH` and the profile hook are deleted. New: the robust mutex (`_GUARD` and `_Txn` tokens), per-tracer monotone `marks`, reconciliation, sys.monitoring tool id 4 or 3 under a per-copy tool name (local events on minted code; global PY_UNWIND only while some section is open, from revision 2), per-mint pending entries, the at-fork handler, `_v5_state()` and `_v5_faultpoints()`. A freed, unowned tool id is re-taken at the next transaction (revision 2). The fork pass-through reads `os.getpid()` (revision 2). Revision 3: the anchor commit and its event toggles move into `_commit`, the first statement of `_run`'s try body, and every clear of PY_UNWIND goes through one `_unwind_off()`. Revision 4: only the opening's own `finally` releases its anchor frame, `_commit` re-tests the claim after its store, and reconciliation prunes dead cores reached from registered anchors (B1). Revision 5 removes revision 4's announcement (`_CLEARING`) and the opener's wait (`_await_clearers`). Every read-decide-write on the event, and every other write styxx makes on its tool id, is instead a *one-call step*: a lazy `itertools`/`operator` pipeline consumed by a single builtin call, which no Python code, thread, signal, finalizer, instrument or greenlet can enter. The anchor test and the clear are then one step, so nothing ever waits at open (M7). Revision 6 corrects this: callback registration is not a one-call step, because `register_callback` runs audit hooks inside it. It is gated per exchange and reports its owner, so at most one exchange can land on another tool's id and that is noted (M7, "The registration"). The bound functions are checked to be C builtins, and tracing is limited to patch levels where the frozen premise gate G_ATOM passed (M0).

rules.section: Target identity > Rule (one sentence)
rules.text: A frame is a *hit* of declared target T iff `frame.f_code is M_T` and `frame.f_globals is F_T.__globals__`, where: - F_T is T's traced function; - M_T is a fresh code object the tracer created at entry with `F_T.__code__.replace()`, published only by assigning it to `F_T.__code__`, and given sys.monitoring local events.

rules.section: Target identity > Rule (one sentence)
rules.text: Attribution then decides whether a hit is credited, and confirmation decides whether it counts.

rules.text: Resolution runs no user code except the import and a module's PEP 562 `__getattr__`, apart from the contrived str-subclass dict-key collision noted in M11. It uses these primitives, all C:

rules.section: Attribution > Rule (one sentence)
rules.text: A hit H is credited to opening O iff all three hold: - at H's entry event (PY_START or PY_RESUME), O's anchor is registered and is met on H's `f_back` chain before the first frame that either has its `f_code` in the cut `_CUT` (every `Handle._run` and `BaseEventLoop._run_once` code seen) or is the anchor of a registered opening whose `loop` is not the thread's running asyncio loop; the running loop is `O.loop` (the *loop boundary*); and no other registered opening of O's tracer is met there (revision 9, GAP-12: revision 8's sentence did not say that a foreign-loop anchor ends the walk, which M6's walk does; M6 is the rule, and this sentence now states it); - H then *confirms*, meaning its frame returns, yields, or unwinds at an offset other than its entry offset; - at that confirmation, O's tracer is still crediting (`id(M_T) in core.by_code`).

rules.section: Attribution > Rule (one sentence)
rules.text: The anchor is the frame of the module-level `_run(core, …)` call, or the `_run_async` coroutine frame, that opened O.

rules.section: Attribution > Rule (one sentence)
rules.text: **The loop boundary (revision 1).** `O.loop` is `asyncio.events._get_running_loop()`, read at O's open through the M1 name `_get_running_loop`.

rules.section: Attribution > Rule (one sentence)
rules.text: It is a C function and runs no user code: from revision 9 (GAP-02) every `coverage_trace()` checks that it is the builtin of the `_asyncio` module before binding it (M0; X156g).

rules.section: Attribution > Rule (one sentence)
rules.text: An event loop started inside a section therefore never credits that section, whatever its dispatch runs through, provided the loop registers itself as the running loop through `asyncio.events._set_running_loop`.

rules.section: Attribution > Rule (one sentence)
rules.text: Every stdlib loop and uvloop does (revision 2, N9).

rules.section: Attribution > Rule (one sentence)
rules.text: A loop that does not, such as a scheduler that drives coroutines by hand, is not an asyncio loop for this rule; it falls under L-WHERE's non-asyncio schedulers.

rules.section: Attribution > Rule (one sentence)
rules.text: The probes show why the cut alone is not enough: - **uvloop.** There is no Python dispatch frame at all.

rules.section: Attribution > Rule (one sentence)
rules.text: In `rev1/p9_uvloop.py` (uvloop 0.22.1, 3.12.3), a `call_soon_threadsafe` job from another thread ran with the section's anchor on its chain and no `Handle._run` frame. - **A pure-Python loop that overrides `_run_once`.** It can run callbacks without `Handle._run` (`rev1/p8_cdispatch.py`).

rules.section: Attribution > Rule (one sentence)
rules.text: In both, the running loop at the hit is the loop started inside the section, not `O.loop`.

rules.section: Attribution > Rule (one sentence)
rules.text: The cut is still needed when dispatch is re-entered on the *same* running loop, such as `loop._run_once()` inside a section opened in a task (`rev1/p17_reentrant_dispatch.py`; X65c).

rules.section: Attribution > Rule (one sentence)
rules.text: **Why the cut holds two codes (revision 2).** With `Handle._run` alone, three routes re-entered stdlib dispatch without a cut frame and without CUT_MOVED: - A1: an override of `TimerHandle._run`; - A2: `asyncio.events.Handle` rebound to a subclass with its own `_run`; - revision 1's R17.

rules.section: Attribution > Rule (one sentence)
rules.text: Every re-entry into the stdlib loop's dispatch runs `BaseEventLoop._run_once`, so its code is now a cut code too.

rules.section: Attribution > Rule (one sentence)
rules.text: `rev2/p1_runonce_cut.py` turns A1, A2 and R17 into `dispatched {f:1}` on 3.12.3 and 3.13.12, with R17's W bound either before or after `__enter__`.

rules.section: Attribution > Rule (one sentence)
rules.text: Plain credit, a section opened inside a task, X65c, X65d, V19b, V61 and V63 keep their outcomes.

rules.section: Attribution > Rule (one sentence)
rules.text: `Handle._run` stays in the cut.

rules.section: Attribution > Rule (one sentence)
rules.text: A loop class with its own `_run_once` that dispatches through `handle._run()` (nest_asyncio's shape) passes no `BaseEventLoop._run_once` frame, and `Handle._run` stops the walk there (`rev2/p2_shared_cut.py`).

rules.section: Attribution > Rule (one sentence)
rules.text: Neither code stops R18: dispatch through code that is neither of them, re-entered on the same loop.

rules.section: Attribution > Why class B cannot reopen through the runtime, and the door that stays open
rules.text: The `f_back` chain holds only frames on the same thread that are executing and waiting on this call. - **Threads.** Threads, pools, executors and daemon threads start at their own bootstrap frame. - **Forked children.** A forked child's thread is not a bootstrap frame.
rules.witness: CPython frame semantics; X82, X83, V35

rules.section: Attribution > Why class B cannot reopen through the runtime, and the door that stays open
rules.text: It is a copy of the forking thread's stack, anchors included (`rev1/p6_fork_chain.py`).

rules.section: Attribution > Why class B cannot reopen through the runtime, and the door that stays open
rules.text: The at-fork handler excludes it: in the child it clears `_ANCHORS` and retires every mint, and the pid pass-through means a child never opens a section or credits one. - **Asyncio, a loop started inside the section.** Its work fails the loop boundary, whatever it dispatches through, uvloop included. - **Asyncio, a loop already running when the section opened.** Its work can reach the section's stack only by re-entering the loop's dispatch.

rules.section: Attribution > Why class B cannot reopen through the runtime, and the door that stays open
rules.text: A re-entry into a stdlib loop's dispatch runs `BaseEventLoop._run_once`, whatever handle class, `Handle._run` binding or `TimerHandle` override is in use.

rules.section: Attribution > Why class B cannot reopen through the runtime, and the door that stays open
rules.text: A loop class that overrides `_run_once` but dispatches through `handle._run()` runs `Handle._run`.

rules.section: Attribution > Why class B cannot reopen through the runtime, and the door that stays open
rules.text: Both codes are in the monotone cut (revision 2), and neither can be minted (RESERVED_TARGET).

rules.section: Attribution > Why class B cannot reopen through the runtime, and the door that stays open
rules.text: A rebinding of either, or a swap of its code, is recorded as CUT_MOVED if any hit or the exit sees it.

rules.section: Attribution > Why class B cannot reopen through the runtime, and the door that stays open
rules.text: One route is left, and only a deliberate harness builds it (R18).

rules.section: Attribution > Why class B cannot reopen through the runtime, and the door that stays open
rules.text: A section opened in a task of a running loop re-enters that loop's dispatch through code that is neither cut code.

rules.section: Attribution > Why class B cannot reopen through the runtime, and the door that stays open
rules.text: Examples are a loop class whose own `_run_once` runs callbacks without calling `Handle._run`, and a replacement of `BaseEventLoop._run_once` that restores the original binding before the hit and dispatches without `Handle._run`; the harness must also call that `_run_once` itself from inside the section.

rules.section: Attribution > Why class B cannot reopen through the runtime, and the door that stays open
rules.text: A section that drains its running loop's `_ready` queue itself, calling each handle's callback directly, is the same route with no loop code at all (revision 3, N4; `critic3/c11_manual_ready_drain.py`: credited).

rules.section: Attribution > Why class B cannot reopen through the runtime, and the door that stays open
rules.text: That shape is L-WHERE's "queues drained inline" (R02), not a new door: the section runs the callback on its own stack.

rules.section: Attribution > Why class B cannot reopen through the runtime, and the door that stays open
rules.text: No library we know of does both: nest_asyncio dispatches through `Handle._run`, and uvloop exposes no re-entrant dispatch.
rules.witness: R18 (outcome pinned; the survey is not testable)

rules.section: Mechanism and lifecycle > M1. Module state
rules.text: Every piece of shared state is one of three kinds: - a registry changed only by single GIL-atomic C operations; - an immutable value replaced by one store; - a monotone map changed only by `setdefault`.
rules.witness: model (its state is these three kinds); model (every commit is one step); G_FI C1-C8; X34b, V61, V62 (monotone cut); model (succession chain)

PY_START, PY_RESUME, PY_RETURN, PY_YIELD, PY_UNWIND = 1, 2, 4, 8, 4096   # revision 9 (GAP-01): literals, sys.monitoring.events' values
_TRACER_ID = "styxx.protocol.coverage_trace/3"
_CACHE_WRAPPER = type(functools.lru_cache(None)(lambda: 0))
_BY_FN   = {}   # F_T -> _Mint            (the key holds F_T; functions hash by identity)
_MINTED  = {}   # id(M_T) -> _Mint        (the mint holds M_T, so the id cannot be reused)
_ANCHORS = {}   # anchor frame -> _Opening (the key holds the frame, so no id reuse)
_CUT     = {}   # id(code) -> code: every Handle._run and BaseEventLoop._run_once code seen; setdefault only
_GUARD   = globals().get("_GUARD", None)   # head of the robust-mutex succession chain; set right after class _Txn (revision 9, GAP-06)
_TOOL    = [None]                          # sys.monitoring tool id; re-validated at every enter
_TOOL_NAME = "styxx.protocol/" + os.urandom(6).hex()   # per loaded copy of the module; the only name adopted
_HANDLE_DICT = [None]                      # asyncio.events.Handle's class dict, read by the first coverage_trace()
_LOOP_DICT = [None]                        # asyncio.base_events.BaseEventLoop's class dict, read with it
_LOST    = []                              # a counter, read as len(_LOST); grows only by list.append, under the mutex (revision 7: a list, so _register can count in C)
_BUSY_SECONDS = 10.0
_LOCAL   = PY_START | PY_RESUME | PY_RETURN | PY_YIELD       # local, on minted code only
# revision 5: the one-call vocabulary (M7), bound once at import; every name is a C callable or a C iterator
_map, _chain, _compress, _filter = map, itertools.chain, itertools.compress, filter
_is, _not, _and, _setitem = operator.is_, operator.not_, operator.and_, operator.setitem
_ARMED   = operator.attrgetter('armed');  _FLAGS = operator.attrgetter('core.flags');  _VALUES = dict.values
_CONSUME = collections.deque(maxlen=0).extend          # consumes an iterator inside one C call
_LOST_KEY, _TRUE = itertools.repeat('UNWIND_LOST'), itertools.repeat(True)
_PYU1, _ZERO1, _NONE1, _NAME1 = (PY_UNWIND,), (0,), (None,), (_TOOL_NAME,)
_repeat, _list = itertools.repeat, list               # revision 6 (M4 i, v): named here; _list is _register's consumer
_is_not, _LOST_APPEND = operator.is_not, _LOST.append   # revision 7 (B1): _register's in-call count
_tee = itertools.tee                                  # revision 8 (M1): _register reads its exchanges through tee
_EVENTS5 = (PY_START, PY_RESUME, PY_RETURN, PY_YIELD, PY_UNWIND)
_CALLBACKS5 = (_on_entry, _on_entry, _on_exit, _on_exit, _on_unwind)   # data: passed to register_callback, never called in a step
_MON     = [None]   # (get_tool, get_events, set_events, set_local_events, register_callback, use_tool_id, get_local_events): bound by the first coverage_trace(); checked at every one (M0; index 6 from revision 9, GAP-03)
_get_running_loop = globals().get("_get_running_loop")   # revision 9 (GAP-02): asyncio.events._get_running_loop, checked and re-bound by every coverage_trace() (M0)
_VERIFIED = ((3, 12, 3), (3, 13, 12))                 # revision 6 (M5): the patch levels on which G_ATOM passed
_monotonic, _sleep = time.monotonic, time.sleep       # revision 5 (N3): the mutex's clock and back-off, bound once

def _on_entry(code, offset):                    # PY_START, PY_RESUME (local, minted code only)
    m = _MINTED.get(id(code))
    if m is None or m.code is not code: return
    f = sys._getframe(1)
    holders = m.holders
    if not _cut_ok():                           # CUT_MOVED: a moved Handle._run or _run_once seen at a hit
        for h in holders: h.flags['CUT_MOVED'] = True
    if f.f_globals is not m.globals:            # CLONE_CALLED: credits nothing
        for h in holders: h.clone_called[id(code)] = m.qualname
        return
    if not _ANCHORS: return                     # no section open anywhere: nothing to credit, PY_UNWIND off (rev. 2)
    out = _outcome(f, code, holders, threading.get_ident())   # the walk: stops at a cut code or a loop boundary
    if out: m.pend[id(f)] = (f, offset, out)   # pending: the only store

rules.section: Mechanism and lifecycle > M7. `_open`, `_commit`, `_run`, `_run_async`, `_detach` (no mutex)
rules.text:
def _run(core, section, fn, args, kwargs):      # module level: its frame is the anchor, its locals hold no facade
    o = _open(core, section, sys._getframe())   # checks and append only (At open, steps 1-6)
    if o is None: return fn(*args, **kwargs)    # forked child: pass-through
    end = "raised"
    try:
        _commit(o)                              # revision 3: inside the try
        result = fn(*args, **kwargs); end = "returned"
    finally:
        _detach(o, (end, ()))                   # no loop in the try body, nor in any function it calls
        o.frame = None                          # revision 4 (B1): the opening's own finally releases the anchor frame
    t = type(result)                            # `is` chain, never `in` (see Resolution)
    if t is GeneratorType or t is CoroutineType or t is AsyncGeneratorType: o.lazy = _lazy_text(result)
    return result
rules.witness: X146c; V47; G_HYG loop clause; H9

rules.text:
def _commit(o):                                 # At open, steps 7-8 (revision 5 order)
    _ANCHORS[o.frame] = o                       # the store; o.frame is set: only this opening's finally releases it
    if 'fin' in o.fin or 'exiting' in o.core.marks:   # step 8: a detacher claimed o, or exit began
        _detach(o, ("open", (OPEN_AT_EXIT_TEXT,)))
        o.core.problems.append(TRACE_INACTIVE_TEXT)
        raise GateSpecError(TRACE_INACTIVE_TEXT)
    _unwind_on(o)                               # one call, after the store: no clear can follow while o is registered
    o.armed = True                              # last: the body may run now

def _register(t):                               # _ensure_tool, M3 step 0, M5 X5. Revision 6: NOT a one-call step
    # ONE STATEMENT, ONE CONSUMING CALL, but register_callback raises an audit event before each exchange, so audit hooks
    # run inside it. { for i in 0..4: if get_tool(t) is not _TOOL_NAME: stop; prev = register_callback(t, ev[i], cb[i]);
    #                  if prev is not cb[i]: _LOST.append(True) }   (revision 7, B1: the count is in the same C call)
    # then owner = get_tool(t); returns [None] * (number of previous callbacks that were not styxx's) + [owner]
    # Revision 8 (M1): the exchanges are read through _tee, whose buffer keeps every prev referenced until the pipeline
    # is released after _list returns, so a replaced callback's finalizer runs only after every count is made.
    get_tool, register_callback = _MON[0][0], _MON[0][4]
    a, b = _tee(_map(register_callback,
                     _compress(_repeat(t), _map(_is, _map(get_tool, _repeat(t, 5)), _repeat(_TOOL_NAME))),
                     _EVENTS5, _CALLBACKS5))
    return _list(_chain(
        _map(_LOST_APPEND, _map(_is_not, _compress(a, _map(_is_not, b, _CALLBACKS5)), _repeat(None))),
        _map(get_tool, (t,))))

rules.section: Mechanism and lifecycle > M9. The at-fork handler
rules.text: Every handler reads the same globals (a reload re-runs the module in the same dict), and a second run finds `_ANCHORS`, `_BY_FN` and `_MINTED` already empty and the id's events already cleared, so the extra runs change nothing.

rules.section: Mechanism and lifecycle > M9. The at-fork handler
rules.text: Revision 2 (N5) orders the steps so that every step that runs no user code comes before any step that can: 1. replace `_GUARD['hint']` with a free token; 2. `_ANCHORS.clear()` (revision 5: `_CLEARING` no longer exists); 3. `set_events(tool, 0)` if the tool is ours; 4. for each mint m in a `list(_MINTED.values())` snapshot: `set_local_events(tool, m.code, 0)` if ours, and `m.pend.clear()`; 5. clear `_BY_FN` and `_MINTED`; 6. last, for each mint in the snapshot: if `m.fn.__code__ is m.code`, restore `m.original`.

rules.section: Mechanism and lifecycle > M9. The at-fork handler

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: **Threat.** An exception can land at any bytecode of the machinery.

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: That includes a function's entry (RESUME) and a loop back-edge.

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: On 3.13, an exception at a back-edge escapes the enclosing `try` table without running `finally` or a with-block's exit (CPython #130279; round-4 found-after item).

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: `rev1/p11_backedge_timer.py` measured this under SIGALRM on 3.13.12. The finally or with-exit was skipped in 400/400 trials for a `while` loop and 188/400 for a `for` loop whose body ends in an `if`. 3.11.15 and 3.12.3 skipped 0. On 3.12.3 the same skip appears at back-edges of code that carries INSTRUCTION, JUMP or BRANCH events (p12, p13), and at the throw-path back-edge of an `await` (p19).

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: **Rule:** no machinery state may depend on a `finally` or with-exit running across a loop, `await` loops included.

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: It also includes the machinery's own callbacks: a sys.monitoring callback is Python code with eval-breaker checks.

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: **Sources:** signal-handler exceptions, KeyboardInterrupt, RecursionError, MemoryError, audit hooks, and a foreign tool raising at an event of one of our frames.

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: That foreign tool can be a lower-id monitoring tool, or a settrace/setprofile function on the thread.

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: Revision 5 (N2) lists every machinery site that raises an audit event, where a raising audit hook is such a source (revision 8's wider self-audit, W2, adds the sites it missed):

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: `object.__setattr__` at every `__code__` write (E4 and `_retire`);

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: `sys._getframe` in `_txn()`, at E0, at X1 and in every `_locked`, and in every callback (`sys._getframe(1)`).

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: A hook that raises on it makes every hit raise out of its callback (L-DELIVERY);

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: (revision 8 self-audit, W2) `sys._getframe` in `_run` and `_run_async`, the argument of `_open` (M7), at every open;

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: (revision 8 self-audit, W2) `builtins.id` at every `id()` call, and `object.__getattr__` at every read of a frame's `f_code` (both raised on 3.12.3 and 3.13.12: `verify8/probe_open_audit.py`, 23 events in one `run()` on `rev8/mech8.py`).

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: The machinery makes such calls in `_open`'s step-5 walk, in every callback (the `_MINTED` lookup, the hit's walk, the pending key and the publication's `id(code) in h.by_code` test), in `_alive`'s liveness test (so inside every reconciliation that tests a holder), and at the mint and retire keys inside E4 and X5. Revision 5's list named neither.

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: Where they land: at open, all before `_open`'s append (steps 1–5), so a hook that raises there propagates out of `run()` (or the coroutine's first step) before any append or store, and fn does not run (V71); in a callback, a raising hook makes that hit raise out of its callback (L-DELIVERY), and one raised at publication loses that one credit, inside I6; inside a transaction, they are further sites of the kind "Audit hooks and slow owners" and I5 describe, which the model's lock-taking and greenlet configurations stand for, and G_FI faults every instruction that makes them;

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: `sys._current_frames` in `_alive`, called by `_acquire` on contention and by every reconciliation's holder test;

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: `gc.get_referrers` in E2's sharing scan and in CLONE_ALIVE;

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: (revision 6, B1) `sys.monitoring.register_callback`, five times inside every `_register`: at E4 (`_ensure_tool`: a first acquisition, an adoption or a rebinding), at M3 step 0 (`_reclaim`, in any transaction after a free), and at X5, which runs on **every exit**, inside the robust mutex.

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: A hook that raises there cuts the registration short (M7, "The registration") and propagates out of the transaction (M5's heading).

rules.text: Revision 5's N2 row said this list named every site; it omitted this one.

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: No one-call step raises an audit event: `_unwind_on`, `_unwind_off`, `_take` and `_set_local` call only `sys.monitoring` functions that raise none (`critic6/a1_audit_monitoring.py`), and G_ATOM checks every gate outcome of each (`rev6/atom6.py`).

rules.text: The close path raises no audit event.

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: The open path raises audit events only before `_open`'s append: `_run`'s `sys._getframe()`, and step 5's `f_code` reads and `id()` calls.

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: (Revision 8 self-audit, W2: this said "the open and close paths still raise no audit event", which `_run`'s frame read and the walk contradict; V71.) `sys._current_frames` costs 3–3.8 µs per call at 51 threads (c5). - **The GIL is assumed.** That is why free-threaded builds refuse. - **Commits are single C operations:** dict setitem, `setdefault`, `pop` and `get` with str, int, frame, function, `_Core` or `_Txn` keys (identity or str hashing, so no Python `__hash__` or `__eq__` runs); `list.append`; `set.clear`; one STORE_ATTR or STORE_SUBSCR; one call of `get_tool`, `get_events`, `set_events`, `set_local_events` or `use_tool_id`; or, from revision 5, one one-call step (M7), which is one C call however many operations it makes inside.

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: A `register_callback` call is *not* such a commit (revision 6): its audit hook runs Python code before its exchange, so `_register` is a sequence of five gated exchanges with Python code possible before each, and M7 states what it guarantees.

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: The one comparison with a foreign object, another tool's name from `get_tool`, is an identity test (`_named`, revision 5), so no foreign `__eq__` runs.

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: The machinery's correctness arguments never use the absence of an eval-breaker check between two bytecodes.

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: They use the order of these operations on each thread, and the fact that nothing runs inside the C call of a one-call step, which calls no Python code and raises no audit event (revision 5; revision 6 restricts the claim to those steps). - **No `try … finally`, no `with` statement and no threading lock** exist anywhere in the machinery, with one exception: `_run`/`_run_async`'s single `try … finally` around fn. - `_run`'s try body is `_commit(o)` and the call of fn, and contains no loop; `_commit` has none either (revision 3).

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: Revision 5: nothing `_commit` or `_detach` calls has a loop either.

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: Revision 4's `_await_clearers` loop is deleted, and a one-call step iterates in C, where there is no bytecode back-edge (`rev5/spec_rev5_eventpath.py`: no backward jump in any of them, both versions).

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: The `finally` itself is `_detach(o, …)` and `o.frame = None`, with no loop. - `_run_async`'s try body is `_commit(o)` and one `await`, whose compiled SEND loop has a throw-path back-edge outside the try range (M7).

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: No count, note, refusal or termination depends on that `finally` running.

rules.section: Exception-safety model
rules.text: If it is skipped, the only machinery state left is a dead anchor, which exit's X3 or a reconciliation pops, and which keeps PY_UNWIND set until then (U4, L-DELIVERY scope). - The only `try … except` clauses are the two user-code sites (the import and PEP 562), which chain into UNRESOLVED, and exit's two `except GateSpecError` clauses around `_locked`, at X0 and X5.

rules.section: Exception-safety model > Invariants preserved by every prefix of every transition
rules.text: **I1: no over-credit.** A count is added to opening O for a frame F of M_T only if all three hold:

rules.section: Exception-safety model > Invariants preserved by every prefix of every transition
rules.text: (a) at F's entry event, O's anchor was registered and met on F's live chain before the cut, the running loop was `O.loop`, O.core held F's mint, and `id(M_T)` was in `O.core.by_code`;

rules.section: Exception-safety model > Invariants preserved by every prefix of every transition
rules.text: (b) F then returned, yielded, or unwound at an offset other than its entry offset;

rules.section: Exception-safety model > Invariants preserved by every prefix of every transition
rules.text: (c) at publication, `id(M_T)` was still in `O.core.by_code`, which exit empties in its first store after the claim.

rules.section: Exception-safety model > Invariants preserved by every prefix of every transition
rules.text: A registered anchor whose frame died (an interrupted close, or a skipped `_run_async` `finally`) can never be on a live chain.

rules.section: Exception-safety model > Invariants preserved by every prefix of every transition
rules.text: A frame killed at its entry never publishes (X135, H8). - **I2: mint integrity.** `fn.__code__ is m.code` only while m is registered with at least one holder that is active or has a live token.

rules.section: Exception-safety model > Invariants preserved by every prefix of every transition
rules.text: The exceptions are inside E4, X5 and `_retire`, and there the next reconciliation repairs the state: holder before register, register before events, events before install; restore before unregister, each step checked by identity. - **I3: reconciled registries.** After any reconciliation: - every registered mint has only live holders; - no mint without a live holder stays registered; - a retired mint has no local events and no pending entries; - global PY_UNWIND is clear if no anchor is registered (M7, U3).

rules.section: Exception-safety model > Invariants preserved by every prefix of every transition
rules.text: Revision 5 makes this hold in every state, not only after a reconciliation, unless an outside party set the event or freed the id.

rules.section: Exception-safety model > Invariants preserved by every prefix of every transition
rules.text: Every reconciliation ends with `_unwind_off(None)`, which repairs that case.

rules.text: Revision 3's version of this clause was false after an open that raced its trace's exit, which left `_ANCHORS[None]` registered for the rest of the process (the fourth critic's B1); revision 4 closes that (At open, steps 8 and 9); - (revision 4) no registered anchor belongs to a dead core (the prune of cores reached from anchors); - no freed, unowned tool id still carries styxx's events or callbacks: step 0 re-takes it (revision 2). - **I4: single finalisation.** Each opening is finalised exactly once, by `o.fin.setdefault`.

rules.section: Version policy
rules.text: interpreter: CPython 3.9, 3.10 | tracing: **refused** (UNSUPPORTED_VERSION at `coverage_trace()` and `__enter__`) | scoring: works | why: There is no sys.monitoring. 3.10's `call_trampoline` runs FastToLocals/LocalsToFast around every Python profile callback. That reverts closure writes made by other threads and keeps deleted locals alive (round-4 BLOCKER), and no Python hook avoids it. D1 also found `importlib.import_module` hanging workers under SIGALRM on 3.10 (8/8). The "3.9 expected like 3.10" line is deleted.

rules.section: Version policy
rules.text: interpreter: CPython 3.11 | tracing: **refused** | scoring: works | why: There is no sys.monitoring. Any Python-level profile hook makes every C call on a sectioned thread skippable, and it leaked the harness's own lock in about 7% of SIGALRM timeouts (see Decisions). This is py310-class corruption of the traced program. Refusing it costs the lab's default interpreter; the P1 retro and the exam run on 3.12/3.13.

rules.section: Version policy
rules.text: interpreter: CPython 3.12.3 and 3.13.12 (GIL builds; `_VERIFIED`) | tracing: **supported**, one mechanism | scoring: works | why: sys.monitoring local events on minted code. The global PY_UNWIND is set only while some section is open (M7, "The unwind scope"; revision 3 corrects revision 1's "while a mint exists" here, MF8). No profile or trace function is ever installed. These are the *verified interpreters*: the patch levels on which G_ATOM passed (M0). A build of the same patch level other than the one G_ATOM ran on is accepted but unverified (M0, N2).

rules.section: Version policy
rules.text: interpreter: every other CPython 3.12.x and 3.13.x (GIL builds) | tracing: **refused** (UNSUPPORTED_VERSION, revision 6) | scoring: works | why: Not a patch level on which the one-call premise was verified. A patch level joins `_VERIFIED` only with a passing G_ATOM run committed beside it (M0, Process gates). Revision 6 said results on other patch levels "are reported as unvalidated"; under M0 no tracing result can be produced there (revision 7, M2).

rules.section: Version policy
rules.text: interpreter: CPython 3.14+, free-threaded builds (`Py_GIL_DISABLED`), other implementations | tracing: **refused** | scoring: works | why: Refused until `Handle._run`, the frame model, sys.monitoring semantics (the RESUME eval-breaker order, PY_UNWIND offsets) and the GIL atomicity argument are re-validated.

rules.section: Version policy
rules.text: **sys.monitoring coexistence.** - **Tool ids.** styxx takes tool id 4, or 3 if 4 is taken, under the per-copy name `_TOOL_NAME`, and holds it until the process exits.

rules.section: Version policy
rules.text: Other tools asking for that id get CPython's ValueError.

rules.section: Version policy
rules.text: If ids 3 and 4 are both held under other names, enter refuses MONITOR_BUSY.

rules.section: Version policy
rules.text: That includes another loaded copy of `styxx.protocol`. - **A freed id.** If a party calls `free_tool_id` on styxx's id, CPython 3.12.3 and 3.13.12 leave its events and callbacks in place (`rev1/p3_free.py`), so the trace keeps counting.

rules.section: Version policy
rules.text: `set_events` on the freed id raises ValueError, so nothing can clear it without re-taking it (`rev2/p3_free_reclaim.py`).

rules.section: Version policy
rules.text: Revision 2 (M3): while the id has no owner, the next transaction re-takes it under `_TOOL_NAME`, which clobbers nobody, and clears its events.

rules.section: Version policy
rules.text: That transaction is normally this trace's own exit.

rules.section: Version policy
rules.text: Exit notes MONITOR_LOST.

rules.section: Version policy
rules.text: In p3, after a free inside a section and a normal exit, revision 1 left 1,000 unwind callbacks for 1,000 unrelated raises, and revision 2 left 0 with the id's events cleared.

rules.section: Version policy
rules.text: If another tool takes the freed id first, styxx never touches it, and styxx's PY_UNWIND callback keeps firing there for the events styxx had set, until that tool changes them (p3: 1,000 of 1,000).

rules.section: Version policy
rules.text: That is disclosed under L-MONITOR and in the R2-B3 row. - **Tools that coexist.** cProfile (PROFILER_ID 2), coverage.py's sysmon core (id 1) and ctrace core (settrace), pdb (settrace), and pure-Python setprofile/settrace tools.

rules.section: Per-finding disposition (all 58 confirmed round-4 findings)
rules.text: Dispositions: - **FIXED**: a mechanism change. - **REFUSED_NOW**: the shape refuses with a coded, remedy-bearing message, disclosed as over-blocking. - **SPEC_TEXT_FIX**: the behaviour is kept and the text is made true. - **DISCLOSED_LIMIT**: a new or widened limit or residual. - **EXAM_CASE_ONLY**: the rule already holds and the exam now pins it. - **RULE_RETIRED**: the rule no longer exists in v5f; a regression case pins the successor behaviour.

rules.text: id: R2-B3 hook persists on a thread | v5f status: CLOSED_S (structural), with one disclosed leak | how: There is no hook. The leftover check requires `sys.getprofile()` and `sys.gettrace()` unchanged on every case thread. A zombie's instrumentation also persists (L-ZOMBIE), but that is not this class. R2-B3 was a silent leak after a *completed* exit. A zombie exists only after a fault has propagated out of the harness's own `with`; `record()` refuses it, and it ends at `__exit__()` or at the next transaction once the facade is dropped. **Revision 2 (M3).** A party that frees styxx's id mid-trace could leave the global PY_UNWIND callback firing after a completed exit. Exit's reconciliation now re-takes an unowned freed id and clears its events (X137 free variant). **Disclosed leak:** if *another tool* takes the freed id before styxx's next transaction, styxx never touches it, and styxx's PY_UNWIND callback keeps firing on that id until the new owner changes its events or callbacks. MONITOR_LOST is noted on the trace in which it happened (`rev2/p3_free_reclaim.py`; L-MONITOR). **Revision 4 (B1).** Revision 3 reopened this class without a fault. An open racing its own trace's exit registered `_ANCHORS[None]`, which no later close could pop, so the process-wide PY_UNWIND callback outlived the completed exit for the rest of the process. That happened in 51–62 of 20,000 natural races per version, and revision 2 did the same with a frame key in 49–69. Closed by the owner-only release of `o.frame`, step 8's re-check after the store, and the reconciliation's prune of cores reached from anchors (At open, steps 8 and 9; M3). Witnesses: X146, X146b, X146c, X146d and X147; `rev4/m1_pairs_modelcheck.py`: no anchor left at any fault-free end state of any pair or triple.

rules.section: Over-blocking, disclosed
rules.text: **Off-stack work never counts.** This covers threads and grandchildren, thread pools, executors, `run_in_executor`, `asyncio.to_thread`, ThreadPool, library worker threads, asyncio child tasks and loop callbacks.

rules.section: Over-blocking, disclosed

rules.section: Over-blocking, disclosed

rules.section: Over-blocking, disclosed

rules.section: Over-blocking, disclosed
rules.text: **Event loops must run outside the section.** `cov.run(name, asyncio.run, main())` counts nothing (X73).

rules.section: Over-blocking, disclosed
rules.text: Every task step and callback of a loop started inside the section fails the loop boundary; with the stdlib loop it is also beyond the cut.

rules.section: Over-blocking, disclosed
rules.text: This holds for uvloop and for any other loop that registers itself through `asyncio.events._set_running_loop` (revision 2, N9; a hand-driven scheduler that does not falls under L-WHERE), and for an eager task factory set through `loop_factory`: `asyncio.run` creates the main task before the loop runs, so the task is not started eagerly, and a `Handle._run` frame lies between it and the section (`rev1/p7_eager_loop_factory.py`, 3.12.3 and 3.13.12).

rules.section: Over-blocking, disclosed
rules.text: A section opened inside a task of a running loop is credited normally, uvloop included (p9).

rules.section: Over-blocking, disclosed
rules.text: **Sections must be calls.** A generator or coroutine returned by fn gets LAZY_RESULT, and whatever of it runs after the close does not count.

rules.section: Over-blocking, disclosed
rules.text: **No same-tracer nesting on one stack above the cut or a loop boundary** (NESTED_SECTION).

rules.text: **What changes in the traced program (revision 2, M4).** This is a change of behaviour, and it is disclosed as one: - Untraced CPython has no eval-breaker check between a `raise` and the matching `except` clause.

rules.section: Stated limits
rules.text: A pending asynchronous exception therefore takes effect only after the handler has started, and the handler's first instructions, up to its first eval-breaker check, always run.

rules.section: Stated limits

rules.section: Stated limits
rules.text: A `with lock:` still releases. - An `except E:` handler for the exception in flight does not start, so its side effects are skipped. - Exception chaining is lost: the new exception's `__context__` is None. - CPython documents no guarantee that a handler starts before a pending asynchronous exception takes effect, but untraced programs can depend on it, and the second critic's probe does.

rules.text: **Instruction sweeps (revision 5).** An *instruction sweep* over a machinery function F on thread T is a family of trials.

rules.section: Exam cases required > Exam harness rules (frozen with the prereg before implementation)
rules.text: Trial k uses a sys.monitoring INSTRUCTION tool on id 5, with local events on `_v5_faultpoints()[F]` filtered to T's live ident.

rules.section: Exam cases required > Exam harness rules (frozen with the prereg before implementation)
rules.text: At the k-th instruction T executes in F, the tool's callback runs the case's *interference* to completion on another thread and waits for it, then returns.

rules.section: Exam cases required > Exam harness rules (frozen with the prereg before implementation)
rules.text: Trials run k = 1, 2, … until a trial in which T executes fewer than k instructions of F; that trial is not counted.

rules.section: Exam cases required > Exam harness rules (frozen with the prereg before implementation)
rules.text: Each trial uses fresh tracers.

rules.section: Exam cases required > Exam harness rules (frozen with the prereg before implementation)
rules.text: The case passes only if every counted trial gives the case's outcome.

rules.section: Exam cases required > Exam harness rules (frozen with the prereg before implementation)
rules.text: No timeout decides anything: the interference is a sequence of complete transitions that never waits for T.

rules.section: Exam cases required > Exam harness rules (frozen with the prereg before implementation)
rules.text: The sweep places the interference between every two consecutive instructions of F, which is where any instrument, signal handler, finalizer or thread switch could run code.

rules.section: Exam cases required > Exam harness rules (frozen with the prereg before implementation)
rules.text: So the sweep is the witness for every rule that says "this read and this write are one call" (the revision-5 row of the mutation audit).

rules.section: Exam cases required > Exam harness rules (frozen with the prereg before implementation)
rules.text: The trial count depends on F's bytecode, which differs between versions and implementations; the outcome does not.

rules.section: Exam cases required > Exam harness rules (frozen with the prereg before implementation)
rules.text: The injector rules below apply to the sweep's tool as well.

rules.text: *No settrace.* A settrace function active over a code object silences other tools' INSTRUCTION events on that code, and they stay silent after `settrace(None)` until `sys.monitoring.restart_events()` (`rev2/p5b_settrace_blinds_injector.py`, 3.12.3 and 3.13.12).

rules.section: Exam cases required > Exam harness rules (frozen with the prereg before implementation)
rules.text: So the injector never runs while a settrace or setprofile function is set, and it calls `restart_events()` before each trial.

rules.section: Exam cases required > Exam harness rules (frozen with the prereg before implementation)
rules.text: If that trial does not fire, the run is void and counts as a failure of the instrument, not as clean.

rules.text: v5e part: X71c | private names read: `P._hook`, and a rebinding of `P._ANCHORS` to a tapping dict | v5f port: Same outcome, NOT_EXERCISED, with the witness tracer's union `{f:1}`. Runs on the main thread before the self-trace. An interval SIGALRM (0.2 ms) is armed before `cov.__exit__()`. Its handler calls f once, the first time `_v5_state()["anchors"]` is below its value when exit began and above 2 (the witness's and G's anchors). By spec order that is inside X3, after X1 and X2, and G's on-stack opening, appended last, is still registered. A handler tripped from inside a monitoring callback cannot be used: code it runs raises no monitoring events (`rev1/p16_handler_events.py`). **Revision 2 (M7): a landing rule instead of hoping for one.** 100,000 suspended `run_async('G', …)` openings make X3 long, not 1,000. A trial *lands* iff the witness tracer's union has f, an observable. A trial that does not land is void and is repeated, up to 20 trials. X71c passes iff some trial lands and no landed trial credits f to G. It fails if no trial lands in 20, or if any landed trial credits G. SM1 applies the same rule to ref+W: a weakening is KILLED iff some landed trial credits G. In `rev2/p7_x71c_landing.py`, 1,000 openings landed in only 6 of 10 trials on 3.12.3, which is the critic's point. 10,000 and 100,000 landed in 10 of 10 on both versions, and the M10 mutant (credit stop after detach) credited G in every landed trial

T2 calls `f(True)`, so f's entry is stored as pending with outcome `u`: f is under no anchor of P on T2. `body` then returns, so section A closes, the last anchor, and PY_UNWIND is cleared. Main sets `go`. f raises on T2, and its unwind is not delivered, so the entry is stranded. T2 catches and drops the exception, and at once calls `f(None)`, which returns. rules.section: The semantic-mutation gate (G_SEM), frozen before implementation, decided by execution
rules.text: **Goal.** Show that the v5f exam detects *weakened* rules, not only deleted refusals.

rules.section: The semantic-mutation gate (G_SEM), frozen before implementation, decided by execution
rules.text: Round 4 found this was not so for v5e: 57/57 deletions were detected, but only 27/63 hand-aimed weakenings, and 29 of the survivors were witnessed exam holes.

rules.section: The semantic-mutation gate (G_SEM), frozen before implementation, decided by execution
rules.text: Equivalence is decided mechanically or by a written argument signed before the freeze, and never by a reviewer after it.

rules.section: The semantic-mutation gate (G_SEM), frozen before implementation, decided by execution
rules.text: **Objectivity rule (revision 1).** Every quantity the gate reads is computed by a frozen script from frozen inputs: the catalog, the corpus, the seeds, N and the list of spec-fixed substrings.

rules.section: The semantic-mutation gate (G_SEM), frozen before implementation, decided by execution
rules.text: No step after the freeze asks a person to judge anything: not whether a mutant is equivalent, whether a line is reachable, which window a fault fell in, or which observables count.

rules.section: The semantic-mutation gate (G_SEM), frozen before implementation, decided by execution > Frozen artifacts
rules.text: The v5f prereg lists `FROZEN_*_SHA256` for each artifact below.

rules.section: The semantic-mutation gate (G_SEM), frozen before implementation, decided by execution > Frozen artifacts
rules.text: All are written by the exam author, who is independent of the implementer (G_INDEP). - **The exam runner.** - **`ref_v5f.py`.** The reference model: an executable spec written **from this document's text alone**.

rules.section: The semantic-mutation gate (G_SEM), frozen before implementation, decided by execution > Frozen artifacts
rules.text: The author attests they did not read `crashcons/v5f_core.py`, `monitor/v5f_region.py` or `narrow/proto`. - **`rules_v5f.json`.** Every normative sentence of this spec as a rule atom with an id, including each crash-consistency ordering and claim (M1–M9, I1–I6). - **`weakenings_v5f.py`** (the SM1 catalog).

rules.section: The semantic-mutation gate (G_SEM), frozen before implementation, decided by execution > Frozen artifacts
rules.text: Each entry is an exact-once text patch against `ref_v5f.py` and carries: rule id, operator family, the NAMED witness case id, the witness's spec outcome, its weakened outcome, and the versions it applies to. - **`opmut_v5f.py`.** The SM2 operator generator for the real implementation. - **`diffprobe_v5f.py`.** The differential probe, its normalizer and its noise-mask procedure. - **`corpus_v5f/`.** The differential-probe corpus, written by the exam author before the freeze.

rules.section: The semantic-mutation gate (G_SEM), frozen before implementation, decided by execution > Frozen artifacts
rules.text: It holds: - every exam case program; - the fuzzer's programs for its frozen seeds; - the crash sweep's points; - the round 1–4 repros, rewritten by the exam author against the public API from `protocol_v5_redteam/round1_module/` through `round4/` and `round4/closure-audit/r1/held_battery.py`.

rules.section: The semantic-mutation gate (G_SEM), frozen before implementation, decided by execution > Frozen artifacts

rules.section: The semantic-mutation gate (G_SEM), frozen before implementation, decided by execution > Frozen artifacts
rules.text: Nothing is added after the freeze. - **`corpus_v5f/manifest.json`** (revision 2, M5).

rules.section: The semantic-mutation gate (G_SEM), frozen before implementation, decided by execution > Frozen artifacts
rules.text: It marks every corpus entry with exactly one comparison class, assigned by a frozen rule from the entry's source and never by judgement: - **`envelope`**: every entry that injects a fault or depends on timing.

rules.section: The semantic-mutation gate (G_SEM), frozen before implementation, decided by execution > Frozen artifacts
rules.text: That is every crash-sweep point; every exam case that uses the id-3 fault tool, the id-5 injector, a signal, `PyThreadState_SetAsyncExc`, a finalizer threshold or a thread race (X71c, X92b, X92c, X131–X133, X135, X138, X139, X140, X140f, X143, X143b, X143c, X144, X145, X146, X146b, X146c, X146d, X146e, X147, X148, X137d, X137e, X138b, X152, X153, X154, X155, V65, V68, R16, the H sweeps and every G_SIG cell; revision 5 retires X149, X149b, X150 and V66); and every fuzzer program whose grammar path includes a fault tool. - **`equality`**: every other entry.

rules.section: The semantic-mutation gate (G_SEM), frozen before implementation, decided by execution > Frozen artifacts
rules.text: At freeze time the manifest is validated on `ref_v5f.py`.

rules.section: The semantic-mutation gate (G_SEM), frozen before implementation, decided by execution > Frozen artifacts

rules.text: An entry that fails this is an exam-author error, fixed before the freeze by reclassifying it under the rule's own terms: it names a timing dependency the rule missed, and the rule is amended. - **`cover_driver_v5f.py`** (revision 2, BF1).

rules.section: The semantic-mutation gate (G_SEM), frozen before implementation, decided by execution > Frozen artifacts
rules.text: Its grammar covers nested tracers, shared and cross-named sections, clones, swaps, generator `throw()`/`close()`, cross-thread coroutine sections, `gc.freeze`, raising targets and lower-id fault tools. - **`sigflood_v5f.py`.** G_SIG: user-lock leaks, hangs, poison, wrong results, and credited ≤ body runs. - **`refcensus_v5f.py`.** G_REF (refusal deletion by coded literal) and G_HYG (hygiene and back-edge lint). - **`controls_v5f.py`.** The positive controls. - **`sm1_result.json`.** Computed at freeze time on `ref_v5f.py`.

rules.text: The row is KILLED only if that invariant is among the sweep's failures; if only other invariants fail, it is WITNESS_MISMATCH: - M1 plain RLock → C3 (hang); - M2 no reconciliation → C7; - M3 register before append → C5 (anchors left); - M4 entering token always live → C7; - M5 exit claim not idempotent → C5 (openings left); - M6 install before register → C5 (code not restored); - M7 exiting token always live → C7; - M10 credit stop after detach → X71c; - M8 (per-thread counters) is RETIRED with `_TH`; M9 is filed as above; - the confirmation weakenings, each with its named witness: publish at entry (X135); unwind-offset check deleted (X135); PY_THROW credited (X119); publication re-check deleted (X71); pending entry keyed without frame identity (V70, revision 8, N2: a deterministic witness, so the row is not UNWITNESSED and EQUIVALENT_BY_SPEC would be false); - coherence weakenings: F_T exempt (X26b); intermediate links exempt (X26d); `'<'` skip widened to "no `__file__`" (X26e); sourceless accepted (X26f); - freeze: "count > 0" or "count ≠ baseline" instead of "count > baseline" (V36b); visible accounting deleted (X58b); - cut and loop: CUT_MOVED only at exit (X141b); E2's refresh deleted (V61); loop boundary deleted in attribution (X65d) or in the NESTED walk (V63); `is` chain replaced by tuple membership (V40b); - revision 2: `_run_once` dropped from the cut (X65g); its binding dropped from `_cut_ok()` (X141c); cut replaced at each E2 (V64); either shareable-code clause deleted (X35b, X35c); PY_UNWIND back to mint scope (H10); `UNWIND_LOST` deleted (X137c); reclaim deleted (X137 free variant); at-fork restores moved first, or pass-through by a cached pid (G_FI fork scenario, C9); - revision 3: `_commit` moved before `_run`'s try (X144); `o.armed` dropped from `_detach`'s check (X143b); the anchor test dropped from it (X143c); the reconciliation's final `_unwind_off` deleted (X143c in revision 3; X137 free variant from revision 5, where no pop leaves a stale event); `_unwind_off` in revision 2's order (X145 (a)); `_retire` step 6 as revision 2's test-then-clear (X145 (b)).

rules.section: The semantic-mutation gate (G_SEM), frozen before implementation, decided by execution > Companion gates
rules.text: The recursion limit is set to 100,000. Each trial calls the step at C depth n, through one `next(map(...))` per level, from a state in which the step has an effect: for `_unwind_off`, the key registered as the last anchor with the event set; for `_unwind_on`, its own anchor registered, the event clear and one armed other opening; for `_take`, the id unowned; for `_set_local`, the id named and the local events different.

rules.section: The semantic-mutation gate (G_SEM), frozen before implementation, decided by execution > Companion gates
rules.text: A binary search over n in [0, 20,000] finds the largest n0 at which the step completes, and the sweep runs n0 − 30 … n0 + 30. It passes iff every trial either completes with the full effect or raises RecursionError with no effect, and both outcomes occur for every step.
